contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #058: Semialgebraic universal covers and bounded domains.

Audit loc:paths and loc:theorem in the September 24, 2026 normal-projective manuscript at their stated generic-center quantifiers. A partial route exclusion is not a full verification or a counterexample.

definitions.kernel: Points with one neighborhood contained in every sufficiently small domain; P_x is its component containing the fixed seed p.
definitions.generic: Outside the permitted countable union of lower-dimensional subanalytic center sets.
definitions.fixed_normalization: D_t^x consists of Z with x+R_t(x)Z in a single fixed locally pseudoconvex subanalytic S; C_t(x,u)=inverse(R_t(x))R_t(x+R_t(x)u).

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 058 (Semialgebraic universal covers and bounded domains.; papers: Semialgebraic universal covers of normal projective varieties; Symmetry of semialgebraic bounded domains with compact quotient; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/058.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Lemma loc:paths: every bounded globally subanalytic open-fiber family with two bounded subanalytic sections in the same component has, locally at generic centers, connecting paths extending holomorphically to one fixed complex center neighborhood, uniformly bounded and uniformly Lipschitz in the path parameter for all small positive scales; all fixed center derivatives have analogous bounds. The section-wide global-subanalytic convention applies to sections; timing need not be subanalytic.

Theorem loc:theorem: for the fixed S, shrinking real invertible R_t, all-bounded-displacement C^k ratio convergence to an everywhere invertible block-diagonal triangular polynomial G_x with G_x(0)=I, and one fixed seed in every open kernel, at generic x every finite L>|p| and eta>0 admit a threshold after which component_p(D_t^x intersect B(0,L)) is within eta of closure(P_x). Bounded-path limits and uniformly initialized nearby starting points have the stated consequences.

Lemma loc:puiseux / prep:puiseux: bounded globally subanalytic functions admit generic joint analytic power parametrizations in the real centers and t^(1/q), with nonzero positive leading units for positive coordinates and common complex neighborhoods on smaller boxes.

The proof of loc:paths obtains finitely many resolved path-graph chart/sign pieces retaining center coordinates and a common monomial scale equation; generically one fixed chain of their compact connected fixed-scale images joins analytic-power-parametrized endpoint lifts, and logarithmic interpolation with a center-independent clock yields the full uniform holomorphic path estimates.

In the proof of loc:theorem the triangular Bishop equations have uniformly persistent C^alpha solutions for each fixed compact schedule homotopy; the complex perturbation center map has full real rank, and the fixed-S continuity principle yields an eventually included center ball.

In the proof of loc:theorem, as the start and transition arcs shrink only after the finite-scale argument, the later-block induction gives u_j tending to zero in every finite L^q and the centers in P_x tend to the limiting path endpoint.

In the proof of loc:theorem, definable bad-center sets for each fixed integer radius and rational accuracy have empty interior by controlled endpoint selection; deleting their lower-dimensional union yields all stated generic-center quantifiers.
There exists an exact counterexample to loc:paths or loc:theorem satisfying every stated hypothesis and defeating the generic conclusion on a nonempty open set of real centers.
The graph-neck family N_(x,t) realizes the fixed-original-domain normalization and the one-dimensional recentering ratio hypotheses of loc:theorem on a nonempty open interval of real centers.

For every abs(x)<1/4, the graph-neck domains N_(x,t) have fixed seed p=(-1,0), endpoint q=(1,0), explicit connecting paths in B(0,2), open kernel abs(y-x*r)<r^2 with -2<r<2, and distance(q,closure(P_x))=1. The conclusion of upper containment fails for this moving-domain family.

The explicit three-piece graph-neck path in research/localization_audit/report.md is holomorphic in complex x on abs(x)<1/2, joins the fixed endpoints through N_(x,t), and has norm plus path-parameter Lipschitz constant less than 6 uniformly in t.

Theorem thm:main: the universal cover of a connected normal projective complex variety has a semialgebraic projective-open presentation if and only if it is biholomorphic to D times C^m times F, where D is a bounded symmetric domain and F is simply connected normal projective, allowing point factors.

The bounded-path retention clause used in Theorem win:construction is justified by applying loc:theorem to the fixed pseudoconvex S, uniform seed ball, and recentering ratio data constructed in sections/windows.tex. This implication does not by itself prove win:construction or thm:main.

external_assumptions.statement: If M is real analytic and f is analytic and not identically zero on any component of M, there are a real analytic manifold N and a proper surjective real analytic map pi:N->M such that f composed with pi is locally normal crossings; pi is locally an isomorphism on a dense open subset of N. This is an absolute theorem, not the relative path estimates.

routes.retired_because: The explicit graph-neck family has uniformly controlled holomorphic-center paths, while its membership inequality contradicts any fixed-S scalar recentering ratio C_t(x,1)->1 with exact margin at least 21/256. It cannot satisfy loc:theorem and is not a counterexample to loc:paths; this excludes only this family.
